rules.title: Clear Value Proposition
rules.description: Within the first screen a newcomer can tell what the product is. Objective check: the opening (the h1 plus the line under it) contains a descriptor of what the product does or is for (a verb phrase such as 'helps', 'lets' or 'turns', an 'is a' statement, or a 'for' phrase), not only a slogan.
rules.confidenceBasis: Admitted 2026-11-22 as documented Avara guidance: measurable pass/fail condition, failing and clean fixtures in test/score-admission.mjs (src/rules/_admissions.json). The cited source is a reference; its passage is not verified.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Quote the opening. In one sentence state what the product is and who it is for, using ONLY the quote. If you cannot, answer fail with the quote. If the opening is only a slogan answer inconclusive.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Rewrite the opening so it answers “what is this, and for whom?” in one sentence, for example: “[Product] helps [audience] [achieve outcome].” Current opening: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: A first-time visitor may not understand what is being offered and leave before reading further. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: An unclear offer lowers the share of visitors who reach the sign-up. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: whether it contains a descriptor (matched phrase)

rules.title: Audience Clarity
rules.description: The opening names who the product is for. Objective check: the h1, subheadline or first-screen text names an audience (a role, team or business type) in a 'for …' or 'helps …' phrase, or addresses one directly.
rules.evaluationPrompt: List every audience named in the quoted opening. If none, answer fail. If the product is plainly for everyone, answer not_applicable.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Name the audience in the opening line, for example “for [role] who [situation]”. The opening currently names no audience: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Visitors who cannot see themselves in the page cannot tell whether it is for them. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Visitors who do not recognise themselves leave, and the ones who stay are less qualified. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Benefit-Focused Messaging
rules.description: Messaging leads with what the visitor gets, not with what the product has. Objective check: among the section headings, count the feature-led ones (feature nouns, 'AI-powered', 'advanced') and the outcome-led ones (outcome verbs, numbers with units). Flag when at least 60% are feature-led and none is outcome-led.
rules.evaluationPrompt: For each quoted heading answer feature or outcome. Flag only if outcome headings are absent. Quote the headings.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Rewrite feature headings as results. Instead of “{{evidence}}”, say what the visitor can now do or stop doing, with a number where you have one.
rules.userImpact: Feature names make the visitor translate what it means for them; some will not. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Feature-first pages tend to read like every competitor's and are harder to choose between. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: each heading with its class (feature / outcome / neutral)

rules.title: Differentiation Clarity
rules.description: Claims of being best are backed by something. Objective check: sentences in the opening that use a superlative or category claim (best, leading, all-in-one, the future of) with no number, customer or source in the same sentence. Real differentiation also needs the owner's positioning, which this check cannot see.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Compare the page's positioning claim with the owner-supplied positioning. If none was supplied, answer inconclusive. Never compare with the wider market.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Replace the unsupported claim with a specific difference you can prove: who you serve that others do not, a number, or a method. Unsupported: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Visitors have heard these claims everywhere and discount them. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Interchangeable claims make price the only way to compare you. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: absence of a number, customer or source in it

rules.title: Headline Effectiveness
rules.description: The headline is a usable length. Objective check: the h1 has 4 to 14 words; 15 to 24 needs a person; over 24 or under 2 fails.
rules.confidenceBasis: Admitted 2026-11-22 as documented Avara guidance: measurable pass/fail condition, failing and clean fixtures in test/score-admission.mjs (src/rules/_admissions.json). The cited source is a reference; its passage is not verified.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Judge only whether the quoted headline can be understood without the page. Quote it.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Tighten the headline to one idea in 4 to 14 words. Current headline ({{observation}}): {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Very long or very short headlines are skimmed past or not understood. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: The headline is the first thing most visitors read; a weak one lowers everything after it. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Supporting Subheadline Quality
rules.description: When a subheadline exists it adds information. Objective check: 8 to 35 words, and not a restatement of the h1 (word overlap under 70%).
rules.confidenceBasis: Admitted 2026-11-22 as documented Avara guidance: measurable pass/fail condition, failing and clean fixtures in test/score-admission.mjs (src/rules/_admissions.json). The cited source is a reference; its passage is not verified.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Quote the subheadline and the h1 and say what the subheadline adds that the h1 does not.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Make the supporting line add what the headline leaves out: who it is for, how it works, or the result. Now: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: A supporting line that repeats the headline wastes the second chance to explain. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: The supporting line is where the specifics belong; leaving them out keeps the offer vague. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Problem Statement Visibility
rules.description: The page names a problem the visitor recognises when the offer depends on one. Objective check: the hero and the next section use problem words (struggle, manual, wasted, without…). Absence is advisory, never a failure.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Quote any sentence that names a problem the visitor has. If none, answer inconclusive.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Name the situation your visitor is in before the solution, in their words (“{{evidence}}”).
rules.userImpact: Without a recognisable problem the visitor may not see why they need this. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Problem recognition is what makes an offer feel necessary. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Outcome-Oriented Messaging
rules.description: The page promises a concrete result. Objective check: the hero and headings contain an outcome (an outcome verb, or a number with a unit such as '2x', '10 minutes', '40%'). A quantified outcome is the strongest pass.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Quote the strongest concrete outcome promised. If none, answer fail.
rules.recommendationTemplate: State the result a visitor can expect, with a number or time if you have one (“Launch in 10 minutes”, “Cut review time by half”). Currently: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: A benefit without a result is hard to picture, so the visitor cannot judge its value. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Concrete outcomes are what justify the price in the visitor's mind. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: outcome phrases found, marked quantified or not

rules.title: Jargon Detection
rules.description: Copy avoids vague buzzwords (including AI buzzwords) that say nothing specific. Objective check: count distinct buzzwords from a maintained lexicon in the h1, subheadline, first-screen text and headings. Flag at 3 or more distinct, or when they make up at least 6% of the first-screen words.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Quote each vague term and say what specific thing it could be replaced with. Do not flag terms that are the product's literal category.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Replace each buzzword with what it actually means for your product: {{evidence}}. Say what happens, to whom, and how much.
rules.userImpact: Buzzwords make visitors work out what is actually being offered, and many will not. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Pages full of the same words look alike, which makes the product easy to dismiss. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: each buzzword and the sentence containing it

rules.title: Above-The-Fold Clarity
rules.description: The first screen on its own explains the offer. Objective check: the h1 is inside the first screen, and so is a supporting line, with at least 15 words of text in the first screen.
rules.confidenceBasis: Admitted 2026-11-22 as documented Avara guidance: measurable pass/fail condition, failing and clean fixtures in test/score-admission.mjs (src/rules/_admissions.json). The cited source is a reference; its passage is not verified.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Looking only at the first screen text, state what is offered. If the first screen has no heading answer fail.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Make the first screen carry a heading and one supporting line that explain the offer without scrolling. Missing: {{observation}}
rules.userImpact: Most visitors decide whether to stay from the first screen alone. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: An empty or unclear first screen raises the share of visitors who leave at once. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: whether the h1 is in the first screen (its top position)

rules.title: Primary Offer Visibility
rules.description: The offer is stated before the page asks for action. Objective check: no call to action sits above the h1 in the first screen.
rules.confidenceBasis: Admitted 2026-11-22 as documented Avara guidance: measurable pass/fail condition, failing and clean fixtures in test/score-admission.mjs (src/rules/_admissions.json). The cited source is a reference; its passage is not verified.
rules.evaluationPrompt: State whether the page asks the visitor to act before explaining the offer. Quote both.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Move the offer statement above the first request to act, or add one line of explanation beside the button. Order found: {{observation}}
rules.userImpact: Being asked to commit before knowing what for feels pushy. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Early requests without context lower trust and clicks. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: position of the first call to action

rules.title: Call-to-Action Context
rules.description: A request for commitment is explained nearby. Objective check: each call to action in the first screen has at least 6 words of explanation in its surrounding block.
rules.evaluationPrompt: For each button quote the sentence that explains it. If none, answer fail.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Put one sentence next to the button saying what happens when it is pressed and what it costs. Unexplained: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: A button with nothing around it leaves the visitor guessing what happens next. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Unexplained buttons are pressed less, or abandoned at the next step. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
requiredEvidence: each first-screen button with the words of context found

rules.title: Message Consistency
rules.description: The page does not contradict itself about the offer. Objective check: the same kind of numeric claim (customers, users, teams, reviews) is stated with two different values in the text.
rules.confidenceBasis: Admitted 2026-11-22 as documented Avara guidance: measurable pass/fail condition, failing and clean fixtures in test/score-admission.mjs (src/rules/_admissions.json). The cited source is a reference; its passage is not verified.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Quote two statements about the same fact that disagree.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Make the numbers agree everywhere, or remove the older one. Conflict: {{evidence}}
rules.userImpact: Two different numbers for the same thing make visitors doubt both. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Inconsistent facts are read as carelessness, which lowers willingness to buy. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Feature Prioritization
rules.description: Features are ordered by the confirmed job to be done. Needs the owner's confirmed job; without it this rule cannot produce a finding.
rules.evaluationPrompt: Compare the feature order with the supplied job. If no job was supplied answer inconclusive.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Reorder the features so the one that does the confirmed job comes first.
rules.userImpact: Visitors scanning for the main capability may stop before reaching it. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: The core capability being buried makes the product look like something else. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: First 5-Second Comprehension
rules.description: Five-second test: show target users the page for five seconds, then ask for unaided recall of the offer and audience. Needs participants.
rules.recommendationTemplate: Run the five-second test with target users and record their words.
rules.userImpact: Shows what visitors actually take away. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: The only direct evidence of first-impression clarity. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
